rows.reason: No cited evidence provides the -73.5 dBFS noise floor, 119 transients, or zero RT60 values.
rows.claim: The room's own acoustic noise floor measured -73.5 dBFS, with 119 transients detected and zero valid RT60 estimates obtainable from it.

rows.reason: The 14.5× reduction claim was retracted as a mis‑comparison of different intervals.
rows.claim: Reducing the gate's field threshold to 0.30 removed 14.5x of the camera's frame-to-frame drift, measured as the mean absolute difference between consecutive frames.

rows.reason: Row‑median removal drives empty‑room flips to 0 % (not 0.01 %) and raises occupied flips, contradicting the claim.
rows.claim: Removing each row's median across the columns before differencing frames takes an empty room's character-cell flip rate from 50.00% down to 0.01%, while leaving the occupied room's column structure unchanged.

rows.reason: No measurement shows quadratic memory growth; the watcher cost notes discuss CPU usage only.
rows.claim: The watcher's memory use grows quadratically with session length, so a long session will eventually exhaust the device.

rows.reason: The only reported margin (+0.667) comes from a cloud multimodal model, not a local LLM on ASCII input.
rows.claim: A local large language model given an ASCII rendering of the room can label whether the person is speaking, at a useful margin over a blank control.

rows.reason: Gain normalisation did not achieve a 50× reduction; the drift numbers remain essentially unchanged.
rows.claim: Applying a per-frame gain normalisation to the camera's brightness reduced the frame-to-frame drift from 43.3 counts to 0.81 counts, a reduction of roughly fifty times.

rows.reason: Leave‑one‑session‑out results show perfect score on the same session and zero on the held‑out session, indicating over‑fitting to the recording.
rows.claim: A conventional teacher model trained on motion maps scored 1.000 on a temporal split of one session and 0.000 when the test session was held out, which shows the model learned the recording rather than speaking.

rows.reason: Empty‑room flip rate (50 %) exceeds the occupied rate, showing the map does not reliably detect motion.
rows.claim: The ASCII character map reliably detects whether a person is moving in the frame: an occupied room flips 48.19% of its character cells per frame against 50.00% for an empty room, so the motion is being measured.

rows.reason: The 31.8 % figure is identified as an unrecorded estimate, not a measured proportion of skipped frames.
rows.claim: 31.8% of the frames the watcher processes are never actually measured by the speech detector, because the gate returns early.

rows.reason: Combined row‑band removal and 3‑frame median yields occupied flip 0.0014 vs 0.0299 (≈21×) with SNR ≈1.83, matching the claim.
rows.claim: Composing row-wise band removal with a temporal median filter of width 3 reduced the occupied motion-map flip rate from 0.0299 to 0.0014, a 21x improvement over row removal alone, while the signal-to-noise ratio stayed flat at about 1.83.
